state.role: ADVISORY prefilter only; Collatz is not proved
state.map: For odd p>=3 and b in {+1,-1}, H_{p,b}(x)=x/2 on even x and (p*x+b)/2 on odd x.
state.word_data: For a primitive binary word w of length m and weight k, B_w=sum_{j:w_j=1}2^j p^(ones after j), D=2^m-p^k, A=abs(D), b=sign(D). For each cyclic rotation r, q_r=B_r/A and h_r is the unique representative in {1,...,2^m} of -b B_r (p^k)^(-1) mod 2^m.
state.proved_background: If A divides B_w, the corresponding integer candidate automatically realizes its parity word and returns. Divisibility is independent of b; positivity selects sign(D)=b.
state.candidate_C1: For every primitive w, if q_r>=h_r for every cyclic rotation r, then A divides B_w.
state.status: ChatGPT Web reported no nonintegral survivor through m<=20, but no proof and no independently verified scan were available when this advisory request was prepared.

c1_stronger_than_positivity.instructions: Is candidate_C1 logically stronger than the classical positivity requirement sign(D)=b, because it imposes one exact lift inequality for every cyclic rotation?

criteria.true: C1 includes constraints not implied merely by sign(D)=b or q_r>0.
criteria.false: C1 is just sign(D)=b or positivity rewritten without additional constraints.

c1_would_bridge_to_integrality.instructions: If candidate_C1 were proved, would it provide a genuine bridge from rotation-wise lift inequalities to denominator divisibility A|B_w?

criteria.true: The conclusion A|B_w is an integrality statement not already assumed in the hypothesis.
criteria.false: The hypothesis already assumes A|B_w or an equivalent condition, making the implication circular.

c1_currently_proved.instructions: Does the supplied state contain a valid general proof of candidate_C1?

criteria.true: A quantified derivation of C1 is present in the supplied state.
criteria.false: Only the statement and finite computational support are present; no general proof is supplied.

single_counterexample_kills_c1.instructions: Would one primitive word satisfying all q_r>=h_r inequalities but failing A|B_w refute candidate_C1?

criteria.true: Such a word satisfies the premise and violates the conclusion.
criteria.false: Such a word would not refute the universally quantified implication.
